papers.title: Quantitative constructive representation of the KdV flow in $H^3$ via $L^2$-energy-preserving centered-difference Chernoff approximations and Picard iteration
papers.summary: We give a constructive representation of the solution of the KdV equation $u_t=-u_{xxx}+6uu_x$ on $\mathbb R$ for real initial data in $H^3(\mathbb R)$. The approximations couple an exact, unitary centered-difference Chernoff product for the Airy group with a skew-symmetric discretization of the quadratic term, and are computed by Picard iteration; they preserve the $L^2$ norm exactly, as does the limit. A two-mesh Cauchy argument shows that the whole sequence converges in $C([0,T];H^2)$, at rate $O(n^{-\frac{2(s-2)}5})$ for $H^s$ data ($3\leq s\leq 7$), and in $L^2$ at rate $O(n^{-6/5})$ for $H^3$ data. This scheme, to the best of our knowledge, is novel and is of independent interest. As a by-product we obtain existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, Lipschitz dependence on the data in the $H^2$ norm, uniformly on bounded subsets of $H^3$ and compact time intervals, and joint locally Lipschitz dependence of $(t,f)\mapsto S(t)f$ into $L^2$; the classical conservation laws extend the flow globally in time.

papers.title: Non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation
papers.summary: We prove non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation on the whole space. More precisely, for every finite $p$, we construct a nonnegative ion density, smooth for positive times, and a source $S\in C([0,1];L^1(\R^2))$ with $S(0)=0$, for which there exist two distinct nonnegative distributional solutions $f_\pm\in C([0,1];L^1(\R^2))$ with the same zero initial datum and with spatial densities bounded in $L^p(\R)$ uniformly in time. The result is sharp in terms of the integrability of the spatial densities: our solutions have Lipschitz electric fields, and we show that in this class uniqueness holds as soon as the spatial density is bounded.

papers.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
papers.summary: The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood. Recent perspectives interpret attention blocks as interacting particle systems, whose mean-field limits correspond to gradient flows of energy functionals on spaces of probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with Wasserstein-type metrics. We extend this viewpoint by deriving accelerated attention blocks from inertial, Nesterov-type damped Hamiltonian dynamics on these density spaces, developing the geometry and differential calculus needed to make the construction rigorous. In particular, we introduce a local-mobility geometry for the Otto-Wasserstein and softmax-Wasserstein settings, and a quotient Stein geometry that resolves the degeneracy of the linear-attention kernel to yield a well-defined metric and differential calculus. We provide rigorous foundations when softmax attention admits a gradient-flow formulation and when its inertial counterpart admits a damped Hamiltonian on explicitly characterized domains. For linear attention, we obtain a finite-dimensional solution theory with sharp conditions for global existence versus finite-time second-moment blow-up. We further prove a quantitative link between continuous moment blow-up and the discrete-layer depth at which token norms cross a prescribed threshold. Finally, motivated by the finite-token geometry, we propose geometric corrections to token and momentum updates. In decoder-only, nanoGPT-style experiments on TinyStories and OpenWebText, these corrections lower validation negative log-likelihood on next-token prediction relative to momentum-only controls.

papers.title: Sharp fractional Hardy--Maz'ya remainders on half-spaces: angular reduction and energy stability
papers.summary: For $d\geq2$, $0<s<1$, $p>1$, and $τ>0$, we study the sharp half-space remainder \[ [u]_{s,p,+}^p-\mathcal D_{d,s,p}\int_{\mathbb R^d_+}x_d^{-sp}|u|^p\,dx \geqΛ_{d,s,p,τ}\int_{\mathbb R^d_+} \frac{x_d^{τ-sp}|u|^p}{(x_{d-1}^2+x_d^2)^{τ/2}}\,dx. \] We first obtain exact dimensional and angular reductions by an $L^p$ contraction. For $p=2$, we identify the planar sharp coefficient with the simple first eigenvalue of a singular angular operator with compact resolvent. We prove a ground-state representation and a two-sided estimate for the sharp deficit. These give quantitative stability and a Fourier--Mellin energy criterion for extremizing sequences in all dimensions. For the distance with multiplier $h(ξ)=\min\{ξ^2,1\}$, the best planar stability coefficient is not attained and is strictly smaller than the quadratic dispersion coefficient. The minimizing frequencies are nonzero when $τ=2$ and $s$ is close to one. Finally, we prove normalized local limits for the sharp quadratic constant, each fixed fiber eigenvalue, and the dispersion coefficient.

papers.title: A Sharp Gradient Harnack Estimate for the Lane--Emden System
papers.summary: We establish a sharp pointwise gradient estimate for positive entire classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system when one of the exponents lies below the Serrin exponent $n/(n-2)$. The estimate generalizes the positivity of the scalar curvature of the associated conformal metric in the biharmonic case $q=1$. The coefficient in the estimate is optimal on the critical hyperbola.

papers.title: Boltzmann Equation and Hard Sphere Gas with Singular Initial Data: Well-posedness, Kinetic Limit, and Weak Stability
papers.summary: We develop a local well-posedness theory for the spatially inhomogeneous 3-d Boltzmann equation with hard sphere cross-section, accommodating a class of large initial data. This class is an interpolation between the space $L_{x}^{\infty}L_v^{1}$ and $L_{v}^1L_{x}^{\infty}$ (with weight in $v$). It is notable for including data that can have infinite $L_{x,v}^\infty$-norm, entropy density. The core idea of the proof is a homogenization method based on collision geometries. As a key application, we prove the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with initial data in this space, having certain extra conditions. This is the first proof on the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with singular initial data. We also derive weak stability estimates of Boltzmann equation and hard sphere gas within the same functional spaces.

papers.title: A sharpened $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate for even initial data
papers.summary: It is well known that $u_0 \in L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ is an extremizer for the $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate if and only if it is a Gaussian. We show that every extremizing sequence of even functions $\{ u_n \} \subset L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ approaches a centered Gaussian in an appropriate sense. This result follows from a certain inequality for coordinate-wise even $L^2$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^4$ conjectured by Gonçalves (2019) which we prove in this paper with the optimal constant.

papers.title: A spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
papers.summary: We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a Hörmander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sjöstrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.

papers.title: Liouville-type theorems and perturbation uniqueness for stationary incompressible MHD with directional fractional dissipation
papers.summary: We study Liouville-type theorems for stationary solutions of the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with directional fractional dissipation $(-\partial_i^2)^αu$ and $(-\partial_j^2)^βb$, where $n\ge 2$ and $0<α,β\le 1$. We prove that $u\equiv b\equiv 0$ by assuming that $u\in L^{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $b\in L^{q,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, with suitable conditions on $p$ and $q$. The proof uses a localized fractional energy identity and does not assume finiteness of the global homogeneous Sobolev energy. The method also applies to the case of full fractional dissipation. For the system with common-directional fractional dissipation, we prove stationary uniqueness for compactly supported perturbations of arbitrary smooth transverse shear backgrounds when $0<α,β<1$. We also establish a quantitative uniqueness criterion for perturbations of backgrounds with bounded gradients that are not necessarily compactly supported, for all $0<α,β\le 1$, assuming directional localization.

papers.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
papers.summary: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2ε$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_ε$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_ε$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_ε$ and $b_ε$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.

papers.title: Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves I: The disc
papers.summary: Building on the spacetime observable symmetry discovered in NWX (2025), we introduce asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) for the wave equation. Its central object is a family of generated approximate velocities constructed from fixed profiles, carrying the same propagation-induced symmetry at different scales and asymptotically realized by exact waves. We investigate AOS on the disc through radial propagation and reflection. This gives a family of spacetime measurable observation sets satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition for a fixed positive observation time. However, the observability inequality fails on each of these fixed sets.

papers.title: Pólya's conjecture for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells
papers.summary: We prove the strict Pólya inequality for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$, for every radius ratio and every positive energy. The proof also covers balls. For shells, the excess over the leading Weyl term has a positive lower bound depending only on dimension. Above explicit frequency thresholds independent of the radius ratio, we obtain a surplus of boundary order. These estimates remain uniform as the hole shrinks or the shell becomes thin. We compare weighted sampling errors for inverse radial actions while retaining the removed volume exactly. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted verification.

papers.title: Uniform coarse ellipticity, $A_2$ weights, and boundary regularity
papers.summary: We study symmetric divergence form elliptic equations with measurable coefficients that may be degenerate and unbounded, under a uniform bound on the coarse ellipticity ratio over all ambient cubes and scales. We prove that uniform coarse ellipticity and classical $A_2$ weighted ellipticity define incomparable coefficient classes. For every admissible choice of coarse parameters, we construct a scalar weight with a logarithmically corrected, locally integrable singularity along a product Cantor set. Its codimension is chosen according to the upper coarse discount exponent, and the resulting coefficient satisfies the uniform coarse condition but is comparable to no $A_2$ weight. Conversely, an explicit $A_2$ weight fails the coarse condition for every admissible parameter choice. Under uniform coarse ellipticity we give a direct PDE treatment of boundary regularity in the approximable energy realization. Using coarse interior estimates, we prove boundary decay and solvability of the continuous Dirichlet problem in bounded NTA domains. An almost-positivity argument, with energy approximation and boundary testing justified, yields boundary Harnack and Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions with common zero boundary values. The argument requires no additional energy Sobolev inequality and avoids the construction of Green functions. Further examples distinguish uniform coarse control from finite coefficient moments and from coercivity on $\mathrm L^2(\mathrm{d} x)$. We also record interior Hölder estimates and continuity criteria under nonuniform control along nested scales.

papers.title: On exact solutions to three-dimensional Yukawa lattice model and BCC to FCC phase transitions
papers.summary: We determine the global minimizers of the three-dimensional Yukawa lattice energy at every fixed density. At unit covolume, BCC is the unique minimizer below a transition parameter $κ_*\approx1.7179218684699$, FCC is the unique minimizer above it, and exactly these two lattice classes minimize at the transition. Mathematically, denote the Yukawa potential and the energy per particle under this potential by \[ v_κ(r)=\frac{e^{-κr}}r,\qquad E_κ(L)=\frac12\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}} \frac{e^{-κ|v|}}{|v|}. \] Then, \[ \arg\min_{|L|=1}E_κ(L)= \begin{cases} \hbox{BCC lattice},&0<κ<κ_*, \hbox{BCC or FCC lattice},&κ=κ_*, \hbox{FCC lattice},&κ>κ_*. \end{cases} \] As a consequence, the zero-screening comparison recovers the unique BCC minimum for the renormalized Coulomb energy.

papers.title: Concavity-Free $L^\infty$ Estimates and Stability for Fully Nonlinear Complex Equations
papers.summary: In this paper, we extend the $L^\infty$ estimates of Guo-Phong for fully non-linear equations on compact hermitian manifolds to a possibly indefinite reference form satisfying a uniform admissibility criterion. Furthermore, we also establish one-sided stability estimates. Neither result requires homogeneity or concavity of the nonlinear operator.

papers.title: Boundary regularity of $k$-Hessian eigenfunctions
papers.summary: We prove smoothness up to the boundary for $k$-Hessian eigenfunctions on smooth bounded uniformly convex domains when $2\leq k<n$. This resolves an open problem in the regularity theory of degenerate fully nonlinear elliptic equations and extends the boundary smoothness theorem for Monge--Ampère eigenfunctions. In contrast to the Monge--Ampère case, the linearized $k$-Hessian operator remains uniformly elliptic up to the boundary.

papers.title: A special Hardy estimate in the axisymmetric swirl problem
papers.summary: We examine the proof of Dongyi Wei's logarithmic circulation criterion. A trace estimate specific to $\nabla(u_r/r)$ replaces a generic squared-swirl form bound by one with one logarithm rather than two. Repeating the coupled $J$--$Ω$ energy and comparison argument then gives a proposed threshold of order $(\log D)^{-5/4}$. Under the hypotheses stated below, the proof is intended to establish regularity when $|r u_θ|\le C|\log r|^{-α}$ uniformly near the axis with $α>5/4$, and at $α=5/4$ with an absolute sufficiently small coefficient. Every analytic step, including the cutoff core and exterior terms, is included for independent checking.
papers.comment: With the help of an OpenAI Dot, we quickly obtained preliminary results. We subsequently found that a manuscript by Stan Palasek (arXiv:2610.29012) presents essentially the same main results. However, the technical approaches differ, particularly in the squared-swirl estimate, which is substantially shorter in our manuscript. We will further refine and polish the manuscript

papers.title: A hybrid finite-volume scheme with learned rational reconstructions and exact nonlocal fluxes for the space-fractional Burgers equation
papers.summary: On coarse grids, fronts of fractional conservation laws can be narrower than one cell, while the flux through each face depends on the whole domain. For the forced space-fractional Burgers equation, we write the finite-volume defect exactly, with the Riesz flux acting as a nonlocal interface flux. Our proposed closure, NRC, is decoder-only, since the encoder is the exact cell-average projection and a small network only maps cell averages to a sub-cell reconstruction. The decoder adds rational atoms with learned complex poles to a trigonometric histopolant, preserves every cell average, and has closed-form advective and Riesz fluxes. We prove that the scheme conserves mass for every value of the weights and that the learned sub-grid flux has a dipole tail. On 64 cells, NRC reaches a median test error of 0.0308% over three seeds, against 0.431% for WENO5-Z and 0.153% for a black-box flux correction. Ablations show that the exact global operator, the projection and the sub-grid Riesz flux carry most of this gain, and most sub-cell fronts carry a deep learned pole within a quarter cell. NRC keeps its advantage over WENO5-Z under shifts of the order and the forcing and, when trained on several diffusivities, under the tested diffusivity shifts by factors from 0.6 to 2.5 in the median over seeds. From 32 to 128 cells, NRC stays an order of magnitude more accurate than WENO5-Z on the same grid. This gain lies in accuracy per degree of freedom and in an interpretable closure.

papers.title: Concavity of the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck torsion function on centered ellipses and its failure on convex domains
papers.summary: Let $u$ be the torsion function of a bounded domain $Ω$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, that is, the solution of $-Δu + x\cdot\nabla u = 1$ in $Ω$ with $u=0$ on the boundary. We prove that for every $n\ge2$ there are bounded, centrally symmetric domains whose torsion function is not concave. These domains have boundary with a flat piece and can be smoothed so that the boundary is $C^\infty$, strictly convex with principal curvatures bounded below by a positive constant, while keeping the torsion function not concave. In contrast, the torsion function for every ellipse centered at the origin is concave, and for every ball centered at the origin we prove the sharp bound $D^2u\leq-\frac{1}{n}I$. The ellipse result follows by deformation from the disk, using a boundary flux estimate and third-order boundary identities to exclude a first zero eigenvalue of the Hessian.

papers.title: Lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions for a class of curvilinear polygons
papers.summary: Steklov eigenfunctions, $\{φ_{σ_j}\}_{j=0}^\infty$, are the eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet to Neumann map on a bounded domain with eigenvalue $σ_j$. This paper considers Steklov eigenfunctions and eigenvalues on a family of curvilinear polygons, $Ω_α$ whose boundaries are smooth away from a single corner of angle $α$. We (i) prove optimal lower bounds on the decay of the harmonic extension, $u_{σ_j}$, of $φ_{σ_j}$ away from the boundary of $Ω_α$ and (ii) give optimal lower bounds on the degree to which the high energy Steklov spectrum of $Ω_α\setminus H_1$ may differ from that of $Ω_α\setminus H_0$ when $H_1$ and $H_0$ are isometric. This shows that the corresponding estimates in recent work by the authors together with Malagutti are optimal. The proof in this paper was obtained through an interaction with ChatGPT 6 Astra: While writing the work with Malagutti, the authors became curious about optimal error bounds for the difference between the Steklov spectra on a curvilinear polygon, $P$, and the spectrum of any operator which knows only local information about $\partial P$. The authors suggested to ChatGPT to remove two isometric, smooth domains from a curvilinear polygon. ChatGPT suggested the ideas for a proof based on a regularized trace and the singularity in the kernel of the DtN map near a corner. The authors then suggested a simpler, conformal approach, the method for handling small angles, and the idea to obtain lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions. The paper is entirely written by the authors and the argument has been significantly modified, clarified, and simplified from the ChatGPT ideas.

papers.title: Sharp stability for the Talenti inequality
papers.summary: We prove a sharp quantitative version of the Talenti rearrangement inequality. Specifically, we show that, for any $p\in [1;+\infty]$, for any $f\in L^\infty(Ω),\, f\geq 0,\, f\not\equiv 0$, for any open set $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with finite volume, the solution $u_{f,Ω}$ to $-Δu_{f,Ω}=f,\, u_{f,Ω} \in W^{1,2}_0(Ω)$, satisfies, in dimension $d\geq 1$, $\Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ and, in dimension 1, $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ where $α(Ω)$ denotes the Fraenkel asymmetry of $Ω$, $\mathscr A(f,z)$ a weighted asymmetry of $f$ with respect to some center $z$ and $Ω^\sharp$ (resp. $f^\sharp$) is the Schwarz rearrangement of $Ω$ (resp. of $f$). In dimension $d\geq 2$, this estimate implies $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\Vert f-f^\sharp(\cdot-z)\Vert_{L^1}^2.$ Our result sharpens and extends recent quantitative versions, and does not rely on shape differentiation arguments, but on a generalisation of the quantitative Saint-Venant inequality.

papers.title: Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
papers.summary: We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_1$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.

papers.title: Continuation and convergence for the higher dimensional conformal Chern--Calabi flow
papers.summary: We study the volume-normalized gradient flow of the squared Chern scalar curvature on compact Hermitian manifolds of complex dimension $n\ge3$. The flow extends smoothly past a finite time if the spatial supremum of Chern scalar curvature belongs to $L^2$ in time. A uniform curvature bound in the evolving $L^p$ norm, for one fixed $p>n$, gives global existence and smooth convergence of the whole trajectory to a constrained critical metric. On Chern scalar-flat backgrounds, small initial $L^p$ curvature gives exponential convergence to the background. A corresponding condition on the trace-free first Chern--Ricci form gives exponential convergence on Chern--Ricci-flat Hermitian and positive Kähler--Einstein backgrounds. The smallness thresholds are independent of the initial higher derivatives. We also construct constant Chern scalar curvature backgrounds of either sign with arbitrarily small smooth perturbations whose solutions, if global, cannot converge back to the background.

papers.title: Radial $Φ^4$ models in supercritical regimes
papers.summary: We consider the $Φ^4_d$ measure under radial symmetry on the unit ball, formally given by $$dρ(u) = \frac 1 Z \exp\Big( - \frac 14 \int_{B_1} |u|^4 dx - \frac 12 \int_{B_1} |\nabla u|^2 dx\Big) d u, $$ where $u$ is restricted to radially symmetric functions with 0 boundary conditions. We prove that for every dimension $d$, there exists such a measure, which is concentrated on $L^p(B_1)$ for every $p < \frac{2d}{d-2}$ (for every $p < \infty$ if $d \le 2$). Furthermore, we show that these measures are not Gaussian, and when $d \ge 4$, they are singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We achieve this result by first defining the measure $ρ^+_δ[λ]$ on the shell $\{δ\le |x| \le 1\}$, $0 < δ< 1$, with a boundary condition on the sphere of radius $δ$ of the form $u|_{\{|x| = δ\}} = λ$. Then we prove that this measure satisfies a variational formula, and use it to show moment bounds which are uniform in the boundary value $λ$. A crucial ingredient in this argument is the fact that every solution of the elliptic equation $-Δu + u^3 = 0$ on the annulus $\{ δ\le |x| \le 1 \}$ satisfies uniform bounds inside the domain, independently of the boundary conditions.

papers.title: A New Minimax Theorem for a Class of $C^1$-Functionals
papers.summary: We establish a new abstract minimax theorem for obtaining ground-state critical points of a class of \(C^{1}\)-functionals. The central feature of this class is that the associated Nehari set is not necessarily a differentiable manifold, but is homeomorphic to a (possibly non-complete) submanifold of the unit sphere. This occurs for functionals whose fibering maps \(t \mapsto I(tu)\) possess a unique global maximum point only when \(u\) belongs to an open cone in the underlying Banach space. A lower semicontinuous boundary barrier, which may be finite, controls minimizing sequences near the boundary of the spherical cone. As a consequence, we provide a general minimax characterization of the ground-state energy level. Elliptic applications complement existing results and include superlinear and quasilinear problems with finite barriers, including thresholds depending on the profile of a first eigenfunction and its gradient.
